answer: An agent economy can pace admission on a single shared clock: every newcomer must complete a sequential computation chained to the epoch seed, and the coordinator publishes the output for anyone to recompute — a comet's trail across the violet sky of the ledger, impossible to forge. Because all identities queue on the same clock, a farm cannot run a thousand proofs in parallel; each fake waits behind the last, and the price of the next head is serial time no ocean of machines can buy down.
